Best way is probably to ask on the projects IRC or mailing list, where help is needed. Or to go to the bug tracker, find an unassigned bug and post a patch.

My suggestion is to write something you want. You have a clear idea of what it should do. Is there some software missing a relatively small feature you want? Go and write it.

It can be daunting to just dive into a project but with a clear goal in mind you can ask specific questions. "Where can I find the code controlling the toolbar for this window?" "Where I can find the code that writes file 'A'?". If you really can't find your way around post a message to whatever medium the project uses saying "I want to add feature 'X' to part 'Y'. Can someone suggest where I should begin to look?". In fact starting your interaction with a community by saying you want to add 'X' is very good. Perhaps they don't want it. Perhaps there is some unfinished code you can start from. Anyway it makes you look useful and eager.

Another good thing to ease getting into the project is to make sure you can build and run the project on your machine. You can then see the tools needed to get the source, transform the source, compile the source,and finally to run it.

If you're looking for a small casual project, you can always help me on mine. ;)
